/-!
# Erdős Problem 785

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/785](https://www.erdosproblems.com/785)
- [ChFa10] Fang, Jin-Hui and Chen, Yong-Gao, *On additive complements*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc.
  (2010), 1923-1927.
- [ChFa11] Chen, Yong-Gao and Fang, Jin-Hui, *On additive complements. II*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc.
  (2011), 881-883.
- [ChFa14] Fang, Jin-Hui and Chen, Yong-Gao, *On additive complements. III*. J. Number Theory
  (2014), 83-91.
- [ChFa15] Chen, Yong-Gao and Fang, Jin-Hui, *On a conjecture of Sárközy and Szemerédi*.
  Acta Arith. (2015), 47-58.
- [Da64] Danzer, L., *Über eine Frage von G. Hanani aus der additiven Zahlentheorie*.
  J. Reine Angew. Math. (1964), 392-394.
- [Er57] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Michigan Math. J. (1957), 291-300.
- [Er61] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Magyar Tud. Akad. Mat. Kutató Int. Közl. (1961),
  221-254.
- [Na59] Narkiewicz, Władysław, *Remarks on a conjecture of Hanani in additive number theory*.
  Colloq. Math. (1959/60), 161-165.
- [Ru17] Ruzsa, Imre Z., *Exact additive complements*. Q. J. Math. (2017), 227-235.
- [SaSz94] Sárközy, A. and Szemerédi, E., *On a problem in additive number theory*.
  Acta Math. Hungar. (1994), 237-245.
-/

open Filter Pointwise
open scoped Topology

namespace Erdos785

/-- The counting function $A(x)=\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert$. -/
noncomputable def counting (A : Set ℕ) (x : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (A ∩ Set.Icc 1 x).ncard

/-- The largest element of $A$ in $[1,x]$, that is $a^*(x)=\max A\cap [1,x]$
(equal to $0$ when there is no such element). -/
noncomputable def aStar (A : Set ℕ) (x : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sSup (A ∩ Set.Icc 1 x)

/-- Two sets $A, B\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ are *exact additive complements* if $A+B$ contains all
large integers and $A(x)B(x)\sim x$. -/
def IsExactAdditiveComplement (A B : Set ℕ) : Prop :=
  IsAdditiveComplement A B ∧
    Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 1)

/--
Let $A,B\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be infinite sets such that $A+B$ contains all large integers.
Let $A(x)=\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert$ and similarly for $B(x)$. Is it true that if
$A(x)B(x)\sim x$ then
$$A(x)B(x)-x\to \infty$$
as $x\to \infty$?

A conjecture of Erdős and Danzer. The answer is yes, proved by Sárközy and Szemerédi [SaSz94],
who actually proved that it is impossible for
$$A(x)B(x)-x=o(A(x)).$$

This was formalized in Lean by van Doorn using Aristotle.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
"https://github.com/Woett/Lean-files/blob/main/ErdosProblem785.lean"]
theorem erdos_785 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite → B.Infinite → IsExactAdditiveComplement A B →
      Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/--
Danzer [Da64] proved that exact additive complements exist (Hanani had earlier conjectured they
do not exist, as reported in [Er57] and [Er61]).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.danzer :
    ∃ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ B.Infinite ∧ IsExactAdditiveComplement A B := by
  sorry

/--
Sárközy and Szemerédi [SaSz94] proved that it is impossible for
$$A(x)B(x)-x=o(A(x)).$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.sarkozy_szemeredi (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (h : IsExactAdditiveComplement A B) :
    ¬ (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) =o[atTop]
      (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
Chen and Fang [ChFa15] proved $A(x)B(x)-x\ll A(x)^c$ cannot hold for any constant $c>0$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.chen_fang (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (h : IsExactAdditiveComplement A B) (c : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) :
    ¬ (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
      (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x : ℝ) ^ c) := by
  sorry

/--
Narkiewicz [Na59] proved that, under the given assumptions (and perhaps swapping $A$ and $B$)
we must have $A(2x)/A(x)\to 1$ and $B(2x)/B(x)\to 2$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.narkiewicz (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (h : IsExactAdditiveComplement A B) :
    (Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A (2 * x) : ℝ) / (counting A x : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 1) ∧
      Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting B (2 * x) : ℝ) / (counting B x : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 2)) ∨
    (Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting B (2 * x) : ℝ) / (counting B x : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 1) ∧
      Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A (2 * x) : ℝ) / (counting A x : ℝ))
        atTop (𝓝 2)) := by
  sorry

/--
Ruzsa [Ru17] has constructed, for any function $w(x)\to \infty$, such a pair of sets with
$$A(x)B(x)-x<w(x)$$
for infinitely many $x$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.ruzsa_upper_bound (w : ℕ → ℝ) (hw : Tendsto w atTop atTop) :
    ∃ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ B.Infinite ∧ IsExactAdditiveComplement A B ∧
      ∃ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ) < w x := by
  sorry

/--
Ruzsa [Ru17] proves that, if $a^*(x)=\max A \cap [1,x]$ and $A$ and $B$ satisfy the conditions
in the problem then (after possibly changing the roles of $A$ and $B$)
$$A(x)B(x)-x > (1-o(1))\frac{a^*(x)}{A(x)}.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.ruzsa_lower_bound (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (h : IsExactAdditiveComplement A B) :
    (∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop,
        (1 - ε) * (aStar A x : ℝ) / (counting A x : ℝ)
          < (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) ∨
    (∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop,
        (1 - ε) * (aStar B x : ℝ) / (counting B x : ℝ)
          < (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
Chen and Fang [ChFa10] proved the stronger statement that $A(x)B(x)-x\to \infty$ if $A$ and $B$
are infinite sets such that $A+B$ contains all large integers and
$$\limsup_{x\to \infty}\frac{A(x)B(x)}{x}<\frac{5}{4}.$$
They later [ChFa14] improved $5/4$ to $3-\sqrt{3}\approx 1.268$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.chen_fang_limsup (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (h : IsAdditiveComplement A B)
    (hlim : limsup (fun x : ℕ => ((counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop
      < ((3 - Real.sqrt 3 : ℝ) : EReal)) :
    Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/--
Chen conjectures that this should be true with $3/2$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.chen_conjecture : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite → B.Infinite → IsAdditiveComplement A B →
      limsup (fun x : ℕ => ((counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop
          < ((3 / 2 : ℝ) : EReal) →
        Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/--
This is sharp, as Chen and Fang [ChFa11] also proved that there exist such $A$ and $B$ with
$$\limsup_{x\to \infty}\frac{A(x)B(x)}{x}=\frac{3}{2}$$
for which $A(x)B(x)-x=1$ for infinitely many $x$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.chen_fang_sharp :
    ∃ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ B.Infinite ∧ IsAdditiveComplement A B ∧
      limsup (fun x : ℕ => ((counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop
          = ((3 / 2 : ℝ) : EReal) ∧
      ∃ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ) = 1 := by
  sorry

end Erdos785

findings.description: The sets may contain zero, and IsAdditiveComplement may use zero as a summand, but counting counts only A ∩ [1,x]. This combination makes the asserted conclusion false, not merely differently normalized. To obtain a counterexample, take Ruzsa's positive exact complements with D(x)=A(x)B(x)−x<log x for unbounded integer x, and use Narkiewicz's dichotomy to label the large member B, so B(x)>√x eventually. Put m=min A and C={a−m : a∈A}. Then C,B are infinite additive complements, and the file counts C by A(n+m)−1. Since counting functions change by at most m over a shift by m and A(n)→∞, C,B still satisfy IsExactAdditiveComplement. However, D_C,B(x−m) ≤ D_A,B(x)−B(x)+m < log x−√x+m along those x. Thus the discrepancy tends to −∞ along a subsequence. The linked formal proof also explicitly requires both sets to exclude zero.
findings.source_evidence: Ruzsa, Exact additive complements, https://arxiv.org/e-print/1510.00812, §1: the sets are 'sets of positive integers'; Theorems 1.1 and 1.3 give the dichotomy and arbitrarily slowly growing upper bound used above. Chen–Fang (2015), p.47, instead allows nonnegative integers but explicitly defines T(x)=|T∩[0,x]|: https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/82737. The cited proof's corollary_erdos_785 has h_pos_A and h_pos_B: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Woett/Lean-files/main/ErdosProblem785.lean.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a consistent convention. Either keep counting over Set.Icc 1 x and require 0 ∉ A and 0 ∉ B, or change counting to (A ∩ Set.Iic x).ncard and update its documentation to count nonnegative integers. The latter is a shared fix for the other discrepancy statements too.

findings.description: The bound concerns the smaller counting function, but the theorem uses counting A with no hypothesis selecting A as the sparse member. IsExactAdditiveComplement is symmetric, so A can be the large member. This is false even for positive sets: Narkiewicz gives A(x)>x^(3/4) eventually after orienting an exact pair this way, while exactness gives |A(x)B(x)−x|≤x eventually. Consequently the discrepancy is O(A(x)^2), contradicting the declaration at c=2. The elementary implication from exactness and x≤A(x)^2 to this Big-O bound was proved in the scratch file without using any sorry-stated theorem.
findings.source_evidence: Chen–Fang (2015), Theorem 0.2, p.48, states A(x)B(x)−x ≥ (min{A(x),B(x)})^M eventually for every M>1: https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/82737. Ruzsa's §1 explicitly says 'For the sequel we will assume ... A is small and B is large' before writing the O(A(x)^c) corollary: https://arxiv.org/e-print/1510.00812.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the comparison function by the c-th power of min (counting A x) (counting B x). Alternatively, add the sparse-side hypothesis Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A (2*x) : ℝ) / counting A x) atTop (𝓝 1), and document the required relabelling.

findings.description: The same unrestricted-zero/positive-only-counting mismatch as in erdos_785 invalidates this universal lower bound. The translated Ruzsa pair described in that finding satisfies all the hypotheses but has negative discrepancy at arbitrarily large arguments. Either disjunct here implies that the discrepancy is eventually strictly positive: take ε=1, making its left-hand side zero. Thus neither disjunct can hold. Allowing the roles to swap does not repair this counterexample.
findings.source_evidence: Ruzsa, https://arxiv.org/e-print/1510.00812, Theorem 1.2, explicitly assumes infinite sets of positive integers and gives the displayed (1−o(1))a*(x)/A(x) lower bound. Theorem 1.3 and Narkiewicz's dichotomy give the counterexample after shifting the sparse set and then omitting its zero from the count.
findings.suggested_fix: Require 0 ∉ A and 0 ∉ B, possibly through a corrected shared exact-complement predicate, or use zero-inclusive counting throughout. The disjunction and the ε/eventually formulation themselves are appropriate.

findings.description: The hypotheses allow zero as a summand while counting excludes it. The translated exact pair from the main finding has normalized product tending to 1, hence its EReal limsup is 1 < 3−√3, so it satisfies hlim as well as complementarity and both infinitude hypotheses. Its discrepancy nevertheless tends to −∞ along a subsequence. Thus this statement also needs a consistent zero/counting convention; using EReal correctly does not address this separate issue.
findings.source_evidence: Chen–Fang (2015), p.47, defines counting over [0,x] for nonnegative sets, and §4, p.57, records their 3−√3 theorem: https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/82737. Chen's 2016 slides, Theorem 5 on p.13, give the same result: https://static.uni-graz.at/fileadmin/veranstaltungen/additive2016/Talks/chen_yg_slides.pdf.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 0 ∉ A and 0 ∉ B if retaining Set.Icc 1 x, or change the shared counting function to Set.Iic x. This theorem uses IsAdditiveComplement directly, so adding positivity only to IsExactAdditiveComplement would not fix it.

findings.description: The proposition whose answer is requested is changed by allowing zero in the summand sets while omitting it from counting. The translated exact pair from the main finding has EReal limsup 1 < 3/2 but fails the required divergence, so the Lean question already has a negative answer for this unintended reason. This is a missing-domain/counting restriction, not evidence that Chen's actual conjecture has been disproved or that its open status is stale.
findings.source_evidence: Chen's 2016 slides define additive complements of nonnegative integers on p.5 and pose Conjecture 2 on p.17: limsup A(x)B(x)/x < 3/2 implies A(x)B(x)−x→∞. https://static.uni-graz.at/fileadmin/veranstaltungen/additive2016/Talks/chen_yg_slides.pdf. The authors' counting convention includes zero, explicitly stated in Chen–Fang (2015), p.47. https://www.erdosproblems.com/785 still records the 3/2 assertion as a conjecture.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep answer(sorry) outside the quantifiers, but either add 0 ∉ A and 0 ∉ B to the quantified hypotheses or use zero-inclusive counting. Do not change the answer or status on the basis of the unintended zero counterexample.

reformulations.difference: The existential exactness statement allows sets containing zero while using positive-only counts, rather than requiring positive sets as in Ruzsa's account of Danzer's result.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For infinite sets write a(n), b(n) for the file's counts and α,β∈{0,1} for membership of zero. Since a,b→∞ and ab/n→1, the zero-inclusive product satisfies (a+α)(b+β)/n=(ab/n)(1+α/a)(1+β/b)→1. Translating both sets upward by one gives positive infinite complements and preserves this normalized limit. Conversely, positive witnesses are already allowed by the Lean statement. Thus this existence assertion, unlike the universal discrepancy bounds, is unaffected.

reformulations.difference: The theorem permits zero even though Ruzsa's presentation of the little-o corollary uses positive sets.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: This little-o impossibility actually holds for any two infinite subsets of ℕ, without complementarity or positivity. At each sufficiently large positive member n of B, the counting product jumps between n−1 and n by at least A(n). A discrepancy that is o(A(x)) at both adjacent arguments cannot accommodate that jump. The stronger assertion and an explicit iff between the positive and unrestricted versions were proved in scratch using no sorry-stated results.

reformulations.difference: The asymptotic factor (1−o(1)) is expressed by ∀ ε>0, eventually (1−ε)H(x)<D(x), with a fixed choice of the set supplying H.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For eventually positive H, an error η(x)→0 with (1−η(x))H(x)<D(x) implies every fixed-ε bound. Conversely the ε bounds imply max(0,1−D(x)/H(x))→0; adding 1/(x+1) to that function supplies an error tending to zero and makes the inequality strict. The outer disjunction correctly makes the role choice once, before ε and the eventual cutoff. This aspect is equivalent; the separately reported zero-domain defect remains.

review.notes: Two independent defects were found. The zero/counting mismatch is listed separately for its four false universal consequences; the Chen–Fang orientation defect persists even for positive sets. All three definitions and ten theorem declarations were checked. Empty/zero cases, finite interval cardinalities and suprema, casts, answer scopes, filter quantifiers and EReal limsups were inspected. Consolidated tests compile without errors or warnings in /workspace/review/scratch.lean; the proved checks have no sorryAx dependency. The full counterexample existence argument uses the cited Ruzsa and Narkiewicz results and is documented in /workspace/review/mathematical-counterexamples.md, rather than being fully formalized in Lean. Full PDFs of Danzer (1964), Sárközy–Szemerédi (1994), and Chen–Fang (2014) were unavailable; their relevant claims were cross-checked in the other primary papers and the authors' slides. No independent stale-status issue was found. The reviewed file was not edited and matches the specified commit byte for byte.

not_demonstrated.reason: The identified counterexample requires Ruzsa's construction of infinite exact complements, then translation and asymptotic estimates. The elementary counting identities alone do not supply a pair satisfying all the theorem's hypotheses.

The previously proved Big-O bound is conditional on eventual x ≤ A(x)^2. Refuting the actual universal declaration also requires constructing an infinite exact-complement pair with that growth, using nontrivial existence and dichotomy results. The repository states those results with sorry, so invoking them would not give an honest self-contained demonstration.
Taking ε=1 simplifies the conclusion to eventual positivity, but a disproof still needs the nontrivial infinite exact-complement counterexample with negative discrepancy at unbounded arguments.

A counterexample must satisfy both infinitude hypotheses, complementarity, and the strict limsup bound. The available finite computations do not establish these premises; the identified counterexample requires the same substantial construction and limit arguments as the main finding.

Refuting the questioned proposition requires an infinite complementary pair with limsup strictly below 3/2 and failure of divergence. The simple binary-digit examples have limsup 3/2 and therefore do not qualify; the identified qualifying construction is not a short Lean proof.

submission.summary: No short, self-contained demonstration of a reported declaration was found. Supporting computations and conditional lemmas are not presented as full disproofs. No trivial_proof.lean file exists; compilation is not applicable.
submission.gave_up_reason: All identified counterexamples require nontrivial infinite exact-complement constructions and asymptotic arguments. Small counting examples miss essential hypotheses, while using the repository's sorry-stated research results would not provide an honest proof. I am therefore taking the permitted bail-out rather than submitting a misleading or substantially longer proof file.

submission.summary: Changed the shared counting function to count A ∩ [0,x], fixing the zero-counting mismatch throughout the statements, and updated the affected documentation. Changed the Chen–Fang comparison to min(A(x), B(x))^c. Answers, references, and status attributes remain unchanged. The requested compilation succeeds with only `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings; additional workspace checks confirm the boundary cases and that aStar needs no change.

/-- The counting function $A(x)=\lvert A\cap [0,x]\rvert$ for a set of nonnegative integers. -/

Let $A,B\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be infinite sets such that $A+B$ contains all large integers.
Let $A(x)=\lvert A\cap [0,x]\rvert$ and similarly for $B(x)$. Is it true that if
$A(x)B(x)\sim x$ then
$$A(x)B(x)-x\to \infty$$
as $x\to \infty$?

A conjecture of Erdős and Danzer. The answer is yes, proved by Sárközy and Szemerédi [SaSz94],
who actually proved that it is impossible for
$$A(x)B(x)-x=o(A(x)).$$

This was formalized in Lean by van Doorn using Aristotle.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
"https://github.com/Woett/Lean-files/blob/main/ErdosProblem785.lean"]
theorem erdos_785 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite → B.Infinite → IsExactAdditiveComplement A B →
      Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/--
Danzer [Da64] proved that exact additive complements exist (Hanani had earlier conjectured they
do not exist, as reported in [Er57] and [Er61]).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.danzer :
    ∃ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ B.Infinite ∧ IsExactAdditiveComplement A B := by
  sorry

/--
Sárközy and Szemerédi [SaSz94] proved that it is impossible for
$$A(x)B(x)-x=o(A(x)).$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.sarkozy_szemeredi (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (h : IsExactAdditiveComplement A B) :
    ¬ (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) =o[atTop]
      (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
Chen and Fang [ChFa15] proved $A(x)B(x)-x\ll \min\{A(x),B(x)\}^c$
cannot hold for any constant $c>0$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.chen_fang (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (h : IsExactAdditiveComplement A B) (c : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) :
    ¬ (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
      (fun x : ℕ => (min (counting A x) (counting B x) : ℝ) ^ c) := by
  sorry

/--
Narkiewicz [Na59] proved that, under the given assumptions (and perhaps swapping $A$ and $B$)
we must have $A(2x)/A(x)\to 1$ and $B(2x)/B(x)\to 2$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.narkiewicz (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (h : IsExactAdditiveComplement A B) :
    (Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A (2 * x) : ℝ) / (counting A x : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 1) ∧
      Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting B (2 * x) : ℝ) / (counting B x : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 2)) ∨
    (Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting B (2 * x) : ℝ) / (counting B x : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 1) ∧
      Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A (2 * x) : ℝ) / (counting A x : ℝ))
        atTop (𝓝 2)) := by
  sorry

/--
Ruzsa [Ru17] has constructed, for any function $w(x)\to \infty$, such a pair of sets with
$$A(x)B(x)-x<w(x)$$
for infinitely many $x$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.ruzsa_upper_bound (w : ℕ → ℝ) (hw : Tendsto w atTop atTop) :
    ∃ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ B.Infinite ∧ IsExactAdditiveComplement A B ∧
      ∃ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ) < w x := by
  sorry

/--
Ruzsa [Ru17] proves that, if $a^*(x)=\max A \cap [1,x]$ and $A$ and $B$ satisfy the conditions
in the problem then (after possibly changing the roles of $A$ and $B$)
$$A(x)B(x)-x > (1-o(1))\frac{a^*(x)}{A(x)}.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.ruzsa_lower_bound (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (h : IsExactAdditiveComplement A B) :
    (∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop,
        (1 - ε) * (aStar A x : ℝ) / (counting A x : ℝ)
          < (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) ∨
    (∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop,
        (1 - ε) * (aStar B x : ℝ) / (counting B x : ℝ)
          < (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
Chen and Fang [ChFa10] proved the stronger statement that $A(x)B(x)-x\to \infty$ if $A$ and $B$
are infinite sets such that $A+B$ contains all large integers and
$$\limsup_{x\to \infty}\frac{A(x)B(x)}{x}<\frac{5}{4}.$$
They later [ChFa14] improved $5/4$ to $3-\sqrt{3}\approx 1.268$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.chen_fang_limsup (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (h : IsAdditiveComplement A B)
    (hlim : limsup (fun x : ℕ => ((counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop
      < ((3 - Real.sqrt 3 : ℝ) : EReal)) :
    Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/--
Chen conjectures that this should be true with $3/2$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.chen_conjecture : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite → B.Infinite → IsAdditiveComplement A B →
      limsup (fun x : ℕ => ((counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop
          < ((3 / 2 : ℝ) : EReal) →
        Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/--
This is sharp, as Chen and Fang [ChFa11] also proved that there exist such $A$ and $B$ with
$$\limsup_{x\to \infty}\frac{A(x)B(x)}{x}=\frac{3}{2}$$
for which $A(x)B(x)-x=1$ for infinitely many $x$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.chen_fang_sharp :
    ∃ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ B.Infinite ∧ IsAdditiveComplement A B ∧
      limsup (fun x : ℕ => ((counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop
          = ((3 / 2 : ℝ) : EReal) ∧
      ∃ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ) = 1 := by
  sorry

end Erdos785
